# Adiox — full reference

> Adiox (https://adiox.io) is a gamified prop-trading and trading-competition platform. Users register, fund one wallet and buy access to prop-firm challenges, tournaments, trading games and a challenge simulator. Every product gives the user a trading account on the Adiox Trading Platform funded with virtual money, checked against its rules every 1–3 seconds. Client portal: https://portal.adiox.io. Trading platform: https://trade.adiox.io. Trade copier: https://copier.adiox.io.

Last updated: 2026-11-27. Prices are in US dollars. Nothing here is investment advice.

## Adiox — Forex Prop Firm, Free Tournaments & Trading Games

URL: https://adiox.io/

Adiox is a forex prop firm and trading competition platform: prop challenges with Pay Later, free forex tournaments, trading games and a $10 simulator.

- What Adiox is: A gamified prop-trading and trading-competition platform with one account and one wallet.
- Products: Challenges, Funded Accounts, Instant Funded, Tournaments, Trading Duels, Trading Battles, Single Player Games and the Training Room.
- Trading accounts: Every product opens an account on the Adiox Trading Platform funded with virtual money.
- Rule checks: Accounts are checked every 1–3 seconds; breaking a rule closes trades and locks the account.
- Cheapest start: First-Buyer Offer: a $5,000 challenge for $4.95. Training Room from $10. Free tournaments.
- Withdrawals: To crypto or bank after KYC, $10 minimum.

Q: What is Adiox?
A: Adiox is a gamified prop-trading and trading-competition portal. You register, fund one wallet and buy access to challenges, tournaments, trading games or the Training Room. Each one gives you a trading account on the Adiox Trading Platform, and the system tracks it live against the rules — you pass or fail, win prizes, or become a funded trader who receives a share of the profit.
Q: Is the money on my trading account real?
A: No. Every product account is funded with virtual money on the Adiox Trading Platform. What is real is the money in your wallet: deposits, prizes, game winnings, funded-account payouts and referral commission.
Q: What happens if I break a rule?
A: The account is eliminated: open trades are closed and the account is locked automatically. Entry fees are not refunded. Tournaments allow a paid rejoin where the organiser has enabled it.
Q: How do I withdraw?
A: Complete identity verification (KYC), then request a withdrawal of at least $10 to crypto or a bank account. The amount is reserved from your balance straight away, you can edit or cancel while it is pending, and our team approves the payout.
Q: Can I practise before buying a challenge?
A: Yes — the Training Room gives you a practice prop-firm account with preset or custom rules from $10. It is pass or fail only, and you can cancel within 5 minutes for a refund.
Q: Where do I trade?
A: On the Adiox Trading Platform web terminal at trade.adiox.io. Use the Start Trading button on any account page in the portal; your login and password are shown there and emailed to you.

## Forex Prop Firm Challenges — Multi-Phase Evaluation | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/challenges/

Forex prop firm challenges on Adiox: pass each phase’s profit target and minimum trading days, later phases free, weekly or monthly payouts, Pay Later option.

- How you pass: Reach the profit target and trade the minimum number of days in each phase.
- Price of later phases: Free — the next phase account is created automatically with the same package.
- Loss rules: Overall loss from the starting balance; daily loss from each day’s opening balance.
- Inactivity: 15 idle days in a row eliminates the account (warnings at 7, 10 and 14 days).
- After passing: A funded-account request is reviewed, then you trade for weekly or monthly payouts.
- Offers: Pay Later, and a one-time $5,000 First-Buyer account for $4.95.

Q: Is there a free prop challenge on Adiox?
A: Challenges have an entry fee, but you can win a free challenge account as a prize in a free tournament. The cheapest paid start is the $4.95 First-Buyer Offer, and Pay Later needs only a small upfront fee. See every free and low-cost option.
Q: Do I pay again for Phase 2?
A: No. When you pass a phase your trades are closed and the next phase account is created automatically for free, using the same package.
Q: When do I pass a phase?
A: When both conditions are met: your equity reaches the profit target and you have traded the minimum number of days. A day counts when your equity changed compared with the previous day.
Q: How is the daily loss measured?
A: From the day's opening balance, recorded at midnight UTC. With a 5% limit on a $10,000 opening balance, equity must stay above $9,500 that day. Profit made earlier in the same day gives you extra room.
Q: What happens if I break a rule?
A: The account is eliminated: open trades are closed and the account is locked. There is no refund of the challenge fee.
Q: Can I stop trading for a while?
A: Up to a point. 15 idle days in a row eliminates the account; you'll receive warnings after 7, 10 and 14 idle days.
Q: What is the payout cycle?
A: You choose weekly (7 days) or monthly (30 days) when you buy the challenge. Each cycle has its own profit-share percentage, shown on the challenge before you pay.

## How to Get Pay Later in Prop Firms — Adiox Pay Later

URL: https://adiox.io/challenges/pay-later/

How to get Pay Later in prop firms: start an Adiox challenge for a small upfront fee and pay the activation fee only after you pass — nothing more if you fail.

- What you pay to start: A small upfront fee.
- What you pay if you pass: The activation fee shown for your account size before you buy.
- What you pay if you fail: Nothing more — no activation fee is due.
- Coupons: Reduce the upfront fee and the activation fee.
- Rules: The same phase rules as any Adiox challenge.
- How to find it: Challenges labelled “Pay Later” in the portal’s challenge list.

Q: Which prop firms let me pay the activation fee only after I pass?
A: On Adiox, Pay Later challenges work this way: you pay a small upfront fee to start, and the activation fee shown at purchase becomes payable only after you pass. If the account doesn't pass, no activation fee is due.
Q: How to get Pay Later in prop firms?
A: Look for challenges sold as "Pay Later" or "pay after you pass", and check two numbers before you buy: the upfront fee and the activation fee due after passing. On Adiox, open the challenges list, pick a challenge labelled Pay Later, and both fees are shown for each account size.
Q: How do I get Pay Later on Adiox?
A: Create a free account, open the challenges list in the portal and choose a challenge labelled Pay Later. Pick the account size, check both fees, and pay the upfront fee at checkout.
Q: Is a Pay Later challenge free to start?
A: No — it needs a small upfront fee. Its advantage is that the larger activation fee is only due if you pass. Check the Promotions page in the portal for any coupon that reduces the fees.
Q: Are the rules easier on Pay Later?
A: No. Pay Later only changes when you pay. Each phase has the same kind of profit target, minimum trading days and loss limits as any other challenge.

## Funded Accounts & Profit-Share Payouts | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/challenges/funded-accounts/

Pass an Adiox challenge to trade a funded account. Request a payout every weekly or monthly cycle and receive profit × your payout share in your wallet.

- Payout amount: Profit × your payout share percentage for the cycle.
- Payout cycle: Weekly (7 days) or monthly (30 days), chosen when you buy the challenge.
- First payout: No waiting period.
- During review: Trading is paused; approval credits your wallet and resets the account.
- Rules: Daily and overall loss limits still apply.

Q: Do I get a new login when I'm funded?
A: No — you keep the same login on a fresh funded account. The trading password is reset and shown on your account page.
Q: Can I trade while a payout is being reviewed?
A: No. Trading is paused while the request is reviewed. After approval the account is reset to its starting balance and you continue with the next cycle.
Q: How is the payout calculated?
A: Profit × your payout share percentage for the cycle you chose. For example, $1,200 profit at an 80% share credits $960 to your wallet.
Q: Is there a waiting period before the first payout?
A: No. The first payout has no waiting period; after that, requests follow your weekly or monthly cycle.

## Instant Funded Challenge — No Profit Target | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/challenges/instant-funded/

Instant Funded is a one-stage Adiox challenge with no profit target. A mandatory 2% single-trade loss limit replaces the evaluation phases.

- Stages: One — no phases.
- Profit target: None.
- Special rule: Any single trade losing 2% of the starting balance eliminates the account.
- Other limits: Daily and overall loss limits still apply.
- Payout condition: The account must be in profit.

Q: Is there a profit target?
A: No. Instant Funded has no profit target and no phases. You keep the account by staying inside the single-trade, daily and overall loss limits.
Q: How is the 2% single-trade limit measured?
A: Against the starting balance. If any single trade loses 2% of the starting balance or more, the account is eliminated.
Q: How do payouts work on Instant Funded?
A: A payout only requires the account to be in profit. Payouts are reviewed by the Adiox team and credited to your wallet, like funded-account payouts.

## Free Forex Tournaments & Trading Competitions | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/tournaments/

Join free forex tournaments and paid trading competitions. Equal starting balance, ranked by final equity, prizes in cash, credit or a challenge account.

- Entry: Free ($0) or paid, shown on each tournament.
- Ranking: Qualifying players ranked by final equity, highest first.
- Qualifying: Minimum number of trades, and the target profit when one is set.
- Prizes: Cash, bonus credit or a free challenge account, by rank range.
- Ties: Tied players share a rank; cash and credit prizes are pooled and split.
- Rejoins: Allowed per tournament for a rejoin fee, with a cooldown and a maximum.

Q: Where can I join a free forex tournament, and how are winners ranked?
A: On Adiox: open the tournaments list in the portal and join any tournament with a $0 entry fee before its cutoff time. Everyone starts with the same balance; at the end, players who made the minimum number of trades (and hit the target, when one is set) are ranked by final equity, highest first, and prizes are paid by rank.
Q: Is this a demo trading contest?
A: Tournament accounts are funded with virtual money, so you never risk your own trading capital. Prizes are real: cash and bonus credit go to your Adiox wallet, and some ranks win a free challenge account.
Q: Can I join after the tournament starts?
A: Until the join cutoff time and while slots are available. If you join before the start, your account waits as pending and switches on when the tournament begins.
Q: How is the daily loss measured in a tournament?
A: From yesterday's closing balance, in dollars. Tournament rules are set as dollar amounts rather than percentages.
Q: Why was I removed from the final ranking?
A: At the end, players who made fewer than the minimum number of trades, or who missed the target profit when one is set, do not qualify for a rank.
Q: When are prizes paid?
A: After the tournament ends and ranks are final. Depending on the tournament, prizes are distributed automatically or by the Adiox team.

## Forex Trading Games — Duels & Multiplayer Battles | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/games/

Forex trading games against friends: 1-vs-1 Trading Duels and multiplayer Trading Battles on virtual-money accounts. The winner takes the pot minus commission.

- Trading Duel: Exactly 2 players; the only Adiox product with a draw.
- Trading Battle: 3 or more players; winner takes all.
- Stake: Set by the lobby creator within the template’s minimum, maximum and step.
- Winner: Paid the pot minus the platform commission.
- No winner: If nobody meets the target, the platform keeps the fees.
- Lobby expiry: 24 hours — then every player is refunded.

Q: Where can I compete against my friends in a simulated forex trading game?
A: On Adiox, create a Trading Duel (1 vs 1) or a Trading Battle (3 or more players). Invitations go to your friends and referrals first. Everyone trades the same starting balance on a virtual-money account for a fixed time, and the winner takes the pot minus commission.
Q: Who sets the entry fee?
A: The player who creates the lobby, within the template's minimum, maximum and step. Everyone who joins pays the same fee.
Q: What does the platform commission cover?
A: The commission percentage is set on each game template and is deducted from the pot before the winner is paid, and from refunds in a Duel draw.
Q: What if nobody reaches the profit target?
A: When a game has a target and nobody meets it, there is no winner and the platform keeps the fees. Check whether a template has a target before you join.
Q: Where are finished games recorded?
A: On the game leaderboard, which lists completed Duels and Battles with the winner, the prize and the commission. Leaderboards →

Q: Do I need to make a profit to pass?
A: Only where the mission says so — the Consistency Challenge requires finishing in profit. Every mission needs at least one closed trade.

Q: Where can I practise forex trading with a profit target and a daily loss limit?

Q: Is there a trading simulator with drawdown rules?
A: Yes — every Training Room simulator enforces a daily and an overall loss limit, and you can add a consistency rule. Breaking a limit fails the simulator, exactly as it would end a real challenge.
Q: Can I win money in the Training Room?

Q: Can I use bonus credit?

## Wallet & Payments — Deposits, Credit, Withdrawals | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/wallet/

Deposit by card, payment link or crypto, withdraw to crypto or bank after KYC ($10 minimum), and see how checkout splits coupon, credit, wallet and card.

- Deposits: Card, payment link or crypto.
- Withdrawals: Crypto or bank, after KYC, $10 minimum.
- Checkout order: Coupon → bonus credit (max 50%) → wallet → payment gateway (min $1).
- Bonus credit: Part of a purchase only; expires after 30 days.
- Failed account creation: The purchase is refunded automatically.

Q: Why do I need KYC to withdraw?
A: Identity verification protects your funds and is required before any withdrawal. You can deposit, play and trade without it. Start it from the KYC page in the portal; the result usually arrives automatically.
Q: Can I withdraw bonus credit?
A: No. Bonus credit can only be used toward part of a purchase, and it expires after 30 days. Only the cash balance is withdrawable.
Q: What happens to my balance when I request a withdrawal?
A: The amount is deducted when you submit the request, so it can't be spent twice. If you cancel while it's pending, or the request is rejected, it goes back to your balance.
Q: Where can I see my history?
A: The wallet section of the portal has separate histories for deposits, withdrawals, deductions, credit received and credit used.

## Adiox FAQ & Glossary — Help Center

URL: https://adiox.io/faq/

Answers about Adiox accounts, wallet, KYC, challenges, funded payouts, tournaments, trading games, the Training Room and rewards, plus a glossary of key terms.

Q: How do I create an account?
A: Register on the portal and confirm your email address — sign-in is blocked until the email is confirmed. Then complete your profile to unlock the $30 welcome credit.
Q: What can I set on my profile?
A: Your nickname, an avatar (choose a built-in one or upload your own), country and state, language and WhatsApp number. Your country and dialling code are suggested automatically. You can change your password from the profile page too.
Q: Why was I signed out?
A: Sessions end after 30 minutes without activity. Pages that refresh live, such as account pages, keep your session alive while they're open.
Q: How can I deposit?
A: By card, by payment link or with crypto. Your wallet is credited when the payment provider confirms the payment, and you'll get an email and a notification.
Q: How do I withdraw?
A: Complete KYC, then request at least $10 to crypto or a bank account. The amount is reserved from your balance immediately; you can edit or cancel while it's pending, and the Adiox team approves and sends the payout.
Q: What is bonus credit?
A: Credit you earn from achievements, the welcome bonus, level rewards, points exchange and some prizes. It can pay for part of a purchase — at most 50% — and expires after 30 days. It can't be withdrawn.
Q: In what order is a purchase paid?
A: Coupon first, then bonus credit up to the cap, then wallet cash, then the payment gateway for anything left (minimum $1). Try the checkout calculator.
Q: What if my account isn't created after I pay?
A: The purchase is refunded automatically.
Q: When do I need KYC?
A: Only for withdrawals. You can register, deposit and use every product without it.
Q: How does verification work?
A: Start a verification session from the KYC page in the portal. The result arrives automatically, and you can refresh the status from the same page.
Q: How do I pass a challenge phase?
A: Reach the phase's profit target and trade the minimum number of days, without breaking the overall or daily loss limit. The next phase is then created for free.
Q: How long can I be inactive?
A: 15 idle days in a row eliminates a challenge account. You'll be warned after 7, 10 and 14 idle days.
Q: How do funded payouts work?
A: When you're in profit and your weekly or monthly cycle has passed, click Request Payout. Trading pauses during review; on approval your wallet receives profit × your payout share and the account resets for the next cycle.
Q: What is the First-Buyer Offer?
A: A one-time $5,000 challenge account for $4.95 for new buyers, protected by email, IP and device checks.
Q: What is Pay Later?
A: A challenge you start with a small upfront fee. An activation fee is shown as payable after you pass, and coupons reduce it too. How Pay Later works.
Q: Is there a free prop challenge?
A: You can win one: free tournaments have a $0 entry fee and their prize tables can award a free challenge account. The cheapest paid start is the $4.95 First-Buyer Offer. See every free and low-cost option.
Q: How are tournament players ranked?
A: By final equity, highest first, among players who qualify. Players with too few trades, or who missed the target profit when one is set, don't qualify.
Q: Can I rejoin after being eliminated?
A: If the tournament allows it: buy a new account for the rejoin fee, up to the maximum number of rejoins, after the cooldown period.
Q: How are tied players paid?
A: Tied players share one rank. Cash or credit prizes for the ranks they cover are pooled and split; a challenge prize goes to each tied player.
Q: What's the difference between a Duel and a Battle?
A: A Duel is exactly two players and can end in a draw. A Battle is three or more players, ranks everyone, and pays only first place.
Q: What if my lobby never fills?
A: A lobby waiting more than 24 hours expires and every player is refunded. The creator can also cancel before the game starts.
Q: What do single player games pay?
A: Bonus credit when you pass the mission. If you fail, there's no reward.
Q: How much does a simulator cost?
A: Custom simulators cost $10 for up to 30 days, $15 up to 40, $20 up to 50 and $25 beyond that. Preset simulators show their price in the portal.
Q: Can I cancel a simulator?
A: Yes, within 5 minutes of starting. The fee is refunded the same way you paid.
Q: How do points and levels work?
A: Claimed achievements give XP. Exchange 100 points for $10 of credit; your level uses lifetime XP, so exchanging never lowers it.
Q: How much referral commission do I earn?
A: 10% of the cash paid by each of your first 20 referred users and 15% from the 21st on. It's paid to your wallet after a short settling delay and reversed if the purchase is refunded.

## How to Choose the Best Forex Prop Firm | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/guides/best-prop-firm/

Find the best prop firm for you: a seven-question checklist for comparing forex prop firms on loss limits, fees, payouts and practice, plus a beginner route.

- Short answer: The best prop firm is the one whose rules you can pass and whose payouts you can collect.
- Compare: Loss-limit measurement, pass condition, fees, payouts, practice, platform, rule breaches.
- For beginners: Rehearse in a simulator, start small, size trades for the daily loss limit.
- Adiox daily loss: Measured from each day’s opening balance at midnight UTC.
- Adiox overall loss: Measured from the starting balance — a fixed floor.

Q: What is the best forex prop firm?
A: There isn't one best firm for everyone. The best forex prop firm for you has loss limits measured in a way you can manage, a pass condition you can meet, transparent fees and published payout terms. Use the seven-question checklist above to compare firms, including Adiox.
Q: Which forex prop firms let me start a challenge before paying in full?
A: Adiox offers Pay Later challenges: you pay a small upfront fee to start and an activation fee only after you pass. New buyers can also start a $5,000 challenge for $4.95.
Q: What is a prop trading platform?
A: A platform where you trade an evaluation or funded account under a firm's rules and earn a share of the profit. On Adiox, every challenge account runs on the Adiox Trading Platform web terminal, and the portal shows each rule's progress live.
Q: Is a prop firm good for beginners?
A: It can be, if you practise the rules first. Beginners fail most often by breaking a daily loss limit. Rehearse in a simulator, start with a small account, and size every trade so one loss can't breach the limit.

## Best Trading Signal Provider: Forex & Gold Guide | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/guides/forex-signal-providers/

How to choose the best trading signal provider for forex or gold (XAUUSD): track record, max drawdown, a stop loss on every signal, reward:risk and red flags.

- Short answer: Choose a long, complete record, a drawdown you can live through and a stop loss on every signal.
- Gold (XAUUSD): Look for wider stops with smaller size, session awareness and news handling.
- Red flags: Hidden losing trades, no stop losses, size increases after losses.
- On Adiox: Top signal providers are listed in the portal’s Trade Copier overview.
- Signals: Adiox doesn’t sell signals; providers are independent.

Q: How can I compare gold signal providers using their trading history and drawdown?
A: Put providers side by side on track-record length, maximum drawdown, stop-loss use on every signal, win rate read with average reward:risk, and consistency across months. Rule out any provider that hides losing trades or increases size after losses. On Adiox, start from the top signal providers listed in the portal's Trade Copier overview.
Q: Who is the best trading signal provider?
A: The best trading signal provider — forex or gold — depends on the drawdown and trading style you can follow. A provider with modest, steady results and a small drawdown is often easier to follow than one with a spectacular month and a deep drawdown. Use the eight-point scorecard on this page.
Q: How do I find the best forex signal provider?
A: Shortlist providers with at least several months of complete history, then compare maximum drawdown, stop-loss use on every signal, and win rate read together with average reward:risk. The best forex signal provider for you is the one whose worst period you could follow without stopping. On Adiox, start from the top signal providers in the portal's Trade Copier overview.
Q: Does Adiox provide trading signals?
A: No. The Adiox portal shows an overview of the top signal providers and masters from the separate copier portal at copier.adiox.io, where providers are independent traders.
Q: Can I copy a signal provider automatically?
A: Copying is done on copier.adiox.io. See the copy trading guide for how master and follower accounts, lot sizing and risk limits usually work.

## How to Do Copy Trading in MT4/MT5 — Setup Guide | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/guides/copy-trading-mt4-mt5/

How to do copy trading in MT4/MT5: master and follower accounts, lot-size modes, symbol mapping and loss limits — and which steps happen on Adiox.

- Setup: Choose a source, connect the follower, set lot sizing, map symbols, set loss limits.
- Lot-size modes: Fixed lot, multiplier, balance ratio or % risk per trade.
- MT5 note: Netting accounts merge positions in the same symbol.
- On Adiox: Find top masters in the portal; copy on copier.adiox.io.
- Prop accounts: Check whether the firm allows copy trading first.

Q: How do I set up copy trading on MT5 and control my lot size?
A: Connect your MT5 follower account with its broker server, login and password, choose the master to copy, then pick a lot-size mode: a fixed lot, a multiplier of the master's lot, a balance ratio, or a percentage of balance risked per trade. Add a maximum lot and a drawdown limit before you switch copying on.
Q: How to do copy trading in MT4/MT5?
A: Choose a master account or signal provider, connect your MT4 or MT5 follower account with its broker server, login and password, pick a lot-size mode, map any differently named symbols, set a maximum lot and a loss limit, then switch copying on. With Adiox, you find top masters in the portal and copy on copier.adiox.io.
Q: How do I copy trades on MT4?
A: The steps are the same as MT5: choose a source, connect the MT4 follower account, set the lot-size mode, map symbols and set loss limits. If your copier runs as an Expert Advisor, the MT4 terminal must stay running.
Q: What is a forex trade copier?
A: Software that reads trades from a source — a master account or a signal provider — and places matching orders on follower accounts, sized by the settings you choose.
Q: Where do I copy trades with Adiox?
A: On the Adiox copier portal at copier.adiox.io. The Adiox client portal shows a read-only overview of top masters, top signal providers and your own masters and copiers.

## How to Pass a Prop Firm Challenge: 9 Steps | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/guides/how-to-pass-prop-firm-challenge/

How to pass a prop firm challenge: size trades for the daily loss limit, know how each limit is measured, spread the target, and rehearse the rules first.

- Short answer: Most challenges are failed on a loss rule, not a missed target — size trades for the daily loss limit.
- Risk per trade: At 1% risk, five losses in a row are needed to hit a 5% daily limit.
- Know the reference: Adiox: daily loss from the day’s opening balance; overall loss from the starting balance.
- Rehearse: Practise the same rules in the Training Room from $10.
- Inactivity: 15 idle days in a row ends an Adiox challenge account.

Q: What is the hardest rule in a prop firm challenge?
A: For most traders it is the daily loss limit, because a single oversized trade or a revenge-trading session can breach it in minutes. Size each trade so several losses in a row stay inside it.
Q: How long does it take to pass a prop firm challenge?
A: At least the minimum number of trading days set by the phase, and as long as you need to reach the profit target without breaking a loss limit. On Adiox, passing Phase 1 creates Phase 2 for free.
Q: Should I practise before buying a challenge?
A: Yes. Rehearsing the exact rules is the cheapest way to find your weak spot. The Adiox Training Room runs a challenge simulator from $10, and you can cancel within 5 minutes for a refund.
Q: What happens if I break a rule?
A: On Adiox the account is eliminated: open trades are closed and the account is locked, with no refund. You can buy a new challenge and start again.

## Daily Loss Limit vs Max Drawdown, Explained | Adiox

URL: https://adiox.io/guides/daily-loss-limit-explained/

Daily loss limit vs max drawdown in prop trading: static, daily-reset and trailing limits with worked $10,000 examples, and how Adiox measures each one.

- Daily loss limit: Caps one day’s losses; resets each day.
- Max drawdown: Caps the total fall for the whole challenge.
- Static vs trailing: Static floors stay put; trailing floors follow your highest balance.
- Adiox daily loss: % of the day’s opening balance, recorded at midnight UTC.
- Adiox overall loss: % of the starting balance — static.

Q: What is a daily loss limit in prop trading?
A: The most an account may lose in a single trading day, usually a percentage of a reference balance. On Adiox challenges it is a percentage of the day's opening balance, recorded at midnight UTC.
Q: What is the difference between daily loss and max drawdown?
A: Daily loss limits one day's losses and resets each day. Max (overall) drawdown limits the total fall from a fixed or trailing reference point for the whole challenge. On Adiox the overall limit is static, measured from the starting balance.
Q: Is a static or trailing drawdown better?
A: A static drawdown gives you more room as you profit, because the floor stays where it started. A trailing drawdown moves up with your highest balance, so your room never grows. Adiox challenges use a static overall limit.
Q: Can I practise with a daily loss limit?
A: Yes — every Adiox Training Room simulator enforces a daily and an overall loss limit, and custom simulators let you choose the percentages.
